topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(1), a licensee's violation of which of the following is also an independent ground for discipline, in addition to violating chapter 18.85 RCW itself or a lawful director rule adopted under it?
choice_a: Chapter 64.36, 19.105, or 18.235 RCW, or RCW 18.86.030, or the rules adopted under those chapters or that section
choice_b: Chapter 82.45 RCW, the real estate excise tax statute
choice_c: Title 11 RCW, the probate code
choice_d: Chapter 59.18 RCW, the residential landlord-tenant act
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(1) makes it a ground for discipline to violate not only chapter 18.85 RCW or the director's rules under it, but also chapter 64.36, 19.105, or 18.235 RCW, or RCW 18.86.030, or the rules adopted under those chapters or that section.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361's introductory clause, upon a finding that any of the statute's enumerated grounds is established, what may the director impose?
choice_a: Any of the sanctions and fines specified in RCW 18.235.110
choice_b: Only outright license revocation, with no lesser sanction ever available
choice_c: A mandatory criminal referral in every case, regardless of severity
choice_d: Sanctions set at the discretion of the local county prosecutor
explanation: RCW 18.85.361 authorizes the director, upon establishing any of the enumerated grounds, to impose any of the sanctions and fines specified in RCW 18.235.110, the Uniform Regulation of Business and Professions Act's sanctions provision.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(2), what type of communication by a licensee is a listed ground for discipline?
choice_a: Making, printing, publishing, or distributing false statements, descriptions, or promises of such a character as to reasonably induce a person to act on them
choice_b: Expressing a licensee's honest personal opinion about general market conditions
choice_c: Making a truthful comparison between two competing active listings
choice_d: Publishing an accurate description of a property's square footage
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(2) lists as a disciplinary ground making, printing, publishing, distributing, or causing to be made false statements, descriptions, or promises of such a character as to reasonably induce a person to act on them.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker's flyer claims a listed property has "zero flood risk, guaranteed," when the broker has no basis for that claim and knows buyers are likely to rely on it in deciding whether to make an offer. This is most directly grounds for discipline under which provision?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(2), false statements or promises reasonably inducing a person to act on them
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(25), the mobile or manufactured home title-transfer ground
choice_c: WAC 308-124B-200, the display-of-licenses rule
choice_d: RCW 18.85.053(4), the title-insurance conditioning ground
explanation: An unsubstantiated, inducing claim like this falls under the false-statements-or-promises ground in RCW 18.85.361(2), not the display, title, or mobile-home provisions.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(3), which of the following is listed as an independent disciplinary ground?
choice_a: Knowingly committing, or being a party to, any material fraud, misrepresentation, concealment, conspiracy, collusion, trick, scheme, or device
choice_b: Completing a continuing education course only one day before the renewal deadline
choice_c: Referring a buyer client to more than one mortgage lender
choice_d: Declining to represent a particular buyer for scheduling reasons
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(3) lists knowingly committing, or being a party to, any material fraud, misrepresentation, concealment, conspiracy, collusion, trick, scheme, or device as a disciplinary ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker fabricates a competing offer to pressure a buyer into raising their bid, then later admits there was no other offer. Which ground for discipline most directly applies?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(3), knowingly committing material fraud, misrepresentation, or a deceptive scheme
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(24), acting as a vehicle dealer without a license
choice_c: WAC 308-124B-200, display of licenses
choice_d: RCW 18.85.361(25), the mobile or manufactured home title-transfer ground
explanation: Fabricating a competing offer to induce a higher bid is a deceptive scheme or trick, squarely within RCW 18.85.361(3)'s material fraud/misrepresentation ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(4), a firm or broker may be disciplined for accepting the services of, or continuing in a representative capacity with, whom?
choice_a: A broker or managing broker who has not been granted a license
choice_b: A licensed appraiser retained to perform a standard appraisal
choice_c: A title company representative delivering promotional material
choice_d: A licensed attorney assisting with closing documents
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(4) makes it a disciplinary ground to accept the services of, or continue in a representative capacity with, a broker or managing broker who has not been granted a license.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A managing broker allows an individual whose real estate license was revoked six months ago to continue showing homes and negotiating offers on the firm's behalf. This most directly exposes the managing broker to discipline under which ground?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(4), accepting the services of, or continuing with, an unlicensed broker
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(14), misrepresenting association membership
choice_c: RCW 18.85.053(2), soliciting a prohibited thing of value from a title company
choice_d: WAC 308-124B-207, firm identification signage
explanation: Continuing to use someone whose license has been revoked falls under RCW 18.85.361(4)'s ground for accepting the services of, or continuing with, an unlicensed broker.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(5), conversion of money, a contract, deed, note, mortgage, or abstract delivered in trust is a disciplinary ground. What creates prima facie evidence of such conversion?
choice_a: Failure to return the item within thirty days of a lawful demand
choice_b: Failure to return the item within ninety days of a lawful demand
choice_c: Failure to return the item before the end of the calendar year
choice_d: Failure to return the item within twenty-four hours of a lawful demand
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(5) provides that failure to return money or a trust document within thirty days of a lawful demand constitutes prima facie evidence of conversion.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(6), a licensee may be disciplined for failing, upon demand, to do what?
choice_a: Disclose information within the person's knowledge, or produce any document, book, or record
choice_b: Attend a mandatory annual firm sales meeting
choice_c: Provide a written apology to a dissatisfied client
choice_d: Complete a self-assessment survey issued by the firm
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(6) lists as a disciplinary ground failing, upon demand, to disclose information within the person's knowledge, or to produce any document, book, or record.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: The director opens an investigation and formally demands that a managing broker produce the firm's transaction files, but the managing broker refuses to turn them over. This refusal is grounds for discipline under which provision?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(6), failing upon demand to disclose information or produce documents, books, or records
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(9), accepting non-cash earnest money without disclosure
choice_c: RCW 18.85.053(3)(c), the title-promotional-material delivery location rule
choice_d: WAC 308-124B-207, firm identification signage
explanation: Refusing to produce records demanded by the director is exactly the conduct barred by RCW 18.85.361(6)'s duty to disclose information or produce documents on demand.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(7), it is a disciplinary ground to continue selling real estate under what circumstance?
choice_a: After the director has, by written order, stated objections to that conduct
choice_b: After a competing broker verbally complains about the listing
choice_c: After a client requests a lower commission rate
choice_d: After the multiple listing service temporarily suspends its website
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(7) makes it a disciplinary ground to continue selling real estate after the director has, by written order, stated objections to that conduct.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(9), accepting something other than cash or its equivalent as earnest money is a disciplinary ground unless what happens?
choice_a: That fact is communicated to the owner
choice_b: The buyer's lender pre-approves the alternative form of payment
choice_c: The earnest money is deposited within twenty-four hours
choice_d: The listing agreement is silent on the form of earnest money
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(9) makes accepting non-cash earnest money a disciplinary ground unless that fact is communicated to the owner.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A buyer offers a promissory note instead of cash as earnest money, and the listing broker accepts it without ever telling the seller. This omission is a disciplinary ground under which provision?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(9), accepting non-cash earnest money without communicating that fact to the owner
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(12), contingent appraisal compensation
choice_c: RCW 18.85.361(24), acting as a vehicle dealer without a license
choice_d: WAC 308-124B-200, display of licenses
explanation: Accepting non-cash earnest money and failing to tell the owner falls squarely within RCW 18.85.361(9).

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(10), a licensee may be disciplined for charging or accepting compensation from more than one party in the same transaction unless what occurs first?
choice_a: Full disclosure is made to all parties involved
choice_b: The additional party is a family member of the licensee
choice_c: The compensation is under five hundred dollars
choice_d: The transaction closes within thirty days
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(10) makes charging or accepting compensation from more than one party in a transaction a disciplinary ground unless full disclosure is first made to all parties.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A managing broker collects a commission from the seller and also accepts an undisclosed referral fee from the buyer's lender on the same transaction, without telling either party. Which ground most directly applies?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(10), accepting compensation from more than one party without full disclosure
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(15), discrimination in real estate brokerage service
choice_c: RCW 18.85.053(3), conditions on delivery of title insurance promotional material
choice_d: RCW 18.85.361(7), continuing to sell after a director's written objection
explanation: Undisclosed compensation from two sides of one transaction is exactly the conduct RCW 18.85.361(10) addresses.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(11), which of the following is listed as a disciplinary ground relating to expenditures on a transaction?
choice_a: Accepting, taking, or charging any undisclosed commission, rebate, or direct profit on expenditures
choice_b: Failing to itemize expenditures in a font larger than ten points
choice_c: Rounding an expenditure to the nearest dollar on a closing statement
choice_d: Paying a vendor invoice one day after its due date
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(11) lists accepting, taking, or charging any undisclosed commission, rebate, or direct profit on expenditures as a disciplinary ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker arranges for a contractor to do repair work on a listed property, and the contractor secretly pays the broker a kickback on the invoice without the seller's knowledge. This is grounds for discipline under which provision?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(11), accepting an undisclosed commission, rebate, or direct profit on expenditures
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(12), contingent appraisal compensation
choice_c: RCW 18.85.361(21), buying or selling property without a written disclosure of licensee status
choice_d: RCW 18.85.053(4), conditioning services on use of a specific title agent
explanation: A secret kickback on a repair invoice is an undisclosed profit on expenditures, barred by RCW 18.85.361(11).

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(12), it is a disciplinary ground to accept employment or compensation for an appraisal of real property under what condition?
choice_a: The compensation is contingent upon the appraiser reporting a predetermined value
choice_b: The appraisal is requested by the buyer rather than the seller
choice_c: The appraisal is completed using a licensed appraiser's standard fee schedule
choice_d: The appraisal takes longer than an industry-standard turnaround time
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(12) prohibits accepting appraisal employment or compensation that is contingent upon reporting a predetermined value.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(13), a broker issuing a report on real property is subject to discipline unless what condition is met?
choice_a: Any interest the broker has in that property is clearly stated in the report
choice_b: The report is issued on firm letterhead
choice_c: The report is co-signed by a second broker
choice_d: The report includes a photograph of the property
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(13) requires a broker issuing a report on real property in which the broker has an interest to clearly state that interest, or face discipline.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker who personally owns a fifteen percent interest in a property issues a market analysis report on that property to a prospective buyer without ever mentioning the ownership interest. This omission is grounds for discipline under which provision?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(13), issuing a report on property in which the broker has an interest without clearly stating that interest
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(14), misrepresenting association membership
choice_c: WAC 308-124B-210(2)(d), advance written approval for an unlicensed brand
choice_d: RCW 18.85.361(19), accepting compensation from other than the licensed firm
explanation: Failing to disclose an ownership interest in a property report is precisely what RCW 18.85.361(13) bars.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(14), which of the following is listed as an independent disciplinary ground?
choice_a: Misrepresentation of membership in any state or national real estate association
choice_b: Failing to renew membership in a local multiple listing service
choice_c: Declining an invitation to join a real estate association
choice_d: Advertising a listing on more than one association's website
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(14) lists misrepresentation of membership in any state or national real estate association as a disciplinary ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker's advertising claims the broker is a "certified member" of a prestigious national real estate association, when in fact the broker's membership lapsed years ago. This false claim is grounds for discipline under which provision?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(14), misrepresentation of membership in a state or national real estate association
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(15), discrimination in hiring or brokerage service
choice_c: WAC 308-124B-210(2)(c), prohibited terms denoting a firm or office
choice_d: RCW 18.85.361(23), the bad-faith catch-all ground
explanation: A false claim of current association membership falls under RCW 18.85.361(14)'s misrepresentation-of-membership ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(15), a licensee may be disciplined for discrimination against any person in what two contexts?
choice_a: Hiring, or in real estate brokerage service activity
choice_b: Scheduling of showings only
choice_c: Selection of a preferred title company only
choice_d: Assignment of parking spaces at the firm's office only
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(15) lists discrimination against any person in hiring or in real estate brokerage service activity as a disciplinary ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(19), a broker or managing broker may be disciplined for accepting a commission or other valuable consideration for a real estate transaction from whom?
choice_a: Any person except the licensed real estate firm with which the broker is associated
choice_b: The firm's designated broker, under any circumstance
choice_c: A client who pays in cash instead of by check
choice_d: The buyer's own lender, if disclosed in writing
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(19) bars a broker or managing broker from accepting a commission or other valuable consideration from any person except the licensed firm with which the broker is associated.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker affiliated with Firm A privately accepts a side payment directly from a buyer, bypassing Firm A entirely, for helping negotiate the deal. This is grounds for discipline chiefly under which rule?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(19), acceptance of compensation from any source other than the licensed firm
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(25), the mobile or manufactured home title-transfer ground
choice_c: WAC 308-124B-210(2)(b), the prohibited legal-entity designation rule
choice_d: RCW 18.85.053(1), the title insurance kickback rule
explanation: A side payment received outside the licensed firm is barred by RCW 18.85.361(19).

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(20), directing any transaction to a lending institution, escrow company, or any other person is a disciplinary ground when done under what circumstance?
choice_a: In expectation of receiving a kickback or rebate from that party, without first disclosing that expectation
choice_b: When the lender offers the buyer the lowest available interest rate
choice_c: When the escrow company's affiliation with the licensee's firm is disclosed in advance
choice_d: When a client independently requests a specific lender by name
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(20) prohibits directing a transaction to a lender, escrow company, or other person in expectation of a kickback or rebate without first disclosing that expectation.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A managing broker routinely refers clients to one particular escrow company because that company privately promises the broker a rebate on closed files, and the broker never tells clients about this arrangement. Which ground for discipline most directly applies?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(20), directing a transaction to an escrow company in expectation of an undisclosed kickback or rebate
choice_b: RCW 18.85.053(3), conditions on delivery of title insurance promotional material
choice_c: RCW 18.85.361(9), accepting non-cash earnest money without disclosure
choice_d: WAC 308-124B-200, display of licenses
explanation: A referral arrangement tied to an undisclosed rebate is exactly what RCW 18.85.361(20) prohibits.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(21), a licensee who buys, sells, or leases real property is subject to discipline unless what disclosure is made?
choice_a: A written disclosure that the person is a real estate licensee
choice_b: An oral disclosure made only if the other party asks
choice_c: A disclosure filed only with the local county assessor
choice_d: No disclosure is ever required for a licensee's own transactions
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(21) requires a licensee who buys, sells, or leases real property to disclose in writing that the person is a real estate licensee.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker personally purchases a distressed property that came across their desk as a listing lead, without ever disclosing in writing to the seller that the buyer is a licensed real estate broker. This omission is grounds for discipline under which provision?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(21), buying real property without a written disclosure of licensee status
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(11), accepting an undisclosed commission or rebate on expenditures
choice_c: RCW 18.85.053(1), the title insurance kickback ground
choice_d: RCW 18.85.361(7), continuing to sell after a director's written objection
explanation: Buying property without disclosing licensee status in writing is exactly the conduct RCW 18.85.361(21) bars.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(23), which broadly worded disciplinary ground can apply even when no other specific ground in the statute exactly fits the licensee's conduct?
choice_a: Any conduct in a real estate transaction which demonstrates bad faith, dishonesty, untrustworthiness, or incompetence
choice_b: Any conduct that a competing firm characterizes as unprofessional
choice_c: Any conduct occurring outside of normal business hours
choice_d: Any conduct involving a transaction under one hundred thousand dollars
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(23) is a catch-all ground covering any conduct in a real estate transaction demonstrating bad faith, dishonesty, untrustworthiness, or incompetence.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A broker's conduct in a transaction does not fit neatly under any of the more specific enumerated grounds in RCW 18.85.361, but a hearing officer finds the broker acted with clear dishonesty toward the client. Under which ground can discipline still be imposed?
choice_a: RCW 18.85.361(23), the catch-all ground for conduct demonstrating bad faith, dishonesty, untrustworthiness, or incompetence
choice_b: RCW 18.85.361(24), the vehicle-dealer ground
choice_c: WAC 308-124B-207, firm identification
choice_d: RCW 18.85.361(25), the mobile or manufactured home title-transfer ground
explanation: The catch-all ground in RCW 18.85.361(23) exists precisely to cover dishonest conduct that does not fit any narrower enumerated ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(24), a real estate licensee is subject to discipline for acting in what unrelated capacity without the proper license?
choice_a: A vehicle dealer
choice_b: A notary public
choice_c: A home inspector
choice_d: An insurance agent
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(24) lists acting as a vehicle dealer without having a license to do so as a disciplinary ground.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.361(25), a licensee engaged in a transaction involving a mobile or manufactured home may be disciplined for failing to ensure what?
choice_a: That title is transferred as required under chapter 46.12 RCW
choice_b: That the home is inspected by a licensed contractor before closing
choice_c: That the home's park space rent is prorated at closing
choice_d: That a home warranty is purchased for the buyer
explanation: RCW 18.85.361(25) makes it a disciplinary ground to fail to ensure that title is transferred under chapter 46.12 RCW in a mobile or manufactured home transaction.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under WAC 308-124B-200, where must the individual licenses of real estate brokers and managing brokers be available?
choice_a: At the address appearing on the individual license
choice_b: At the Department of Licensing's headquarters only
choice_c: In a locked file cabinet inaccessible to visitors
choice_d: Wherever the broker personally keeps a vehicle registration
explanation: WAC 308-124B-200 requires that licenses of real estate brokers and managing brokers be available at the address appearing on the individual license.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under WAC 308-124B-200, how must firm and branch office licenses be displayed?
choice_a: In an area visible to the public
choice_b: Only upon a client's specific written request
choice_c: Behind the reception desk, out of public sightline
choice_d: Only during the firm's annual license renewal period
explanation: WAC 308-124B-200 requires that all firm and branch office licenses be displayed in an area visible to the public.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under WAC 308-124B-207, a real estate firm or branch office must be identified how, at the address appearing on the license?
choice_a: By displaying the name of the firm or the assumed name as licensed, visible to the public
choice_b: By displaying only the designated broker's personal name
choice_c: By displaying a generic "Real Estate Office" sign with no firm name
choice_d: No display is required if the office operates by appointment only
explanation: WAC 308-124B-207 requires a firm or branch office to be identified by displaying the name of the firm or the assumed name as licensed, visible to the public, at the address appearing on the license.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: How does the firm-identification requirement of WAC 308-124B-207 differ in scope from the advertising requirement of WAC 308-124B-210?
choice_a: WAC 308-124B-207 requires visible signage identifying the firm at its licensed office address, while WAC 308-124B-210 requires the firm name to appear across all advertising and solicitation media, including internet, email, and print
choice_b: WAC 308-124B-207 applies only to online advertising, while WAC 308-124B-210 applies only to physical office signage
choice_c: The two rules are identical and apply to the exact same conduct
choice_d: WAC 308-124B-207 applies only to managing brokers, while WAC 308-124B-210 applies only to designated brokers
explanation: WAC 308-124B-207 is a physical-signage requirement at the licensed office address, while WAC 308-124B-210 is a broader advertising-media requirement covering all promotional channels.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Under RCW 18.85.053(2), real estate licensees and those with a controlling interest in a real estate business are prohibited from soliciting or accepting what from a title insurance company, agent, or its representative?
choice_a: Anything of value that the title insurance company, agent, or representative is legally prohibited from offering
choice_b: A standard, publicly available marketing brochure about title insurance products
choice_c: A business card exchanged at a networking event
choice_d: A copy of the title company's published rate schedule
explanation: RCW 18.85.053(2) bars licensees from soliciting or accepting anything of value from a title insurance company, agent, or representative that the entity is legally prohibited from offering.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: A candidate is reviewing the enumerated grounds in RCW 18.85.361 and must identify the option that is NOT actually one of them. Which of the following is NOT a listed ground?
choice_a: Failing to wear a name badge at all times while showing property
choice_b: Conversion of money or documents delivered in trust
choice_c: Discrimination against any person in hiring or brokerage service
choice_d: Acting as a vehicle dealer without a proper license
explanation: RCW 18.85.361 contains no name-badge requirement; the other three options are all enumerated grounds in the statute.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: On an exam question listing four possible disciplinary grounds, only three actually appear in RCW 18.85.361. Which option is the one that does NOT appear in the statute?
choice_a: Failing to achieve a minimum annual sales quota set by the firm
choice_b: Accepting non-cash earnest money without communicating that fact to the owner
choice_c: Issuing a property report without disclosing the broker's own interest in the property
choice_d: Misrepresentation of membership in a state or national real estate association
explanation: RCW 18.85.361 sets no sales quota requirement; the other three options are all enumerated grounds in the statute.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Advertising Compliance & Disciplinary Oversight
question: Of the four items below, three are genuine disciplinary grounds under RCW 18.85.361 and one is not. Which one is NOT a genuine ground under the statute?
choice_a: Using a personal vehicle older than ten years to transport clients
choice_b: Charging compensation from more than one party without full disclosure
choice_c: Directing a transaction to a lender in expectation of an undisclosed kickback
choice_d: Continuing to sell real estate after the director's written objection
explanation: RCW 18.85.361 has no vehicle-age requirement; the other three options are all enumerated grounds in the statute.
